//: Composite indexes AURIX's queries need.
Firestore creates single-field indexes automatically, so most queries here
need nothing — including the catalogue search. That one filters on a
single array field (`searchTokens`, with `array-contains`) and applies no
second filter and no ordering, so the automatic array index serves it.
It is listed under fieldOverrides below only to make the array indexing
explicit and to document the query it exists for, not because the default
would be wrong.
The one query that genuinely needs a composite index is the import
de-duplication lookup: findBySource filters on `source` and `sourceId`
together, and a two-field equality filter needs a composite index or it
fails at runtime with a link to create one.
Declaring them here means a fresh project has them after
`firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes` rather than after the first
import fails.
Deliberately absent: an index on likedTracks(createdAt), on
playlists(updatedAt), or on playlistTracks(position). Those are
single-field orderings and are automatic.
The catalogue search index.
`searchTokens` holds up to 180 prefix strings per song, and the
array-contains query in FirestoreCatalogService.search is what makes a
keystroke an indexed lookup instead of a collection scan.
ARRAY_CONFIG is what supports array-contains. ASCENDING/DESCENDING
ordering on this field is switched off deliberately: nothing orders by
it, and each one would be another 180 index entries written per song.
The same, for playlist name search. Playlist documents carry a much
smaller token array — one name rather than a title, artist and album.
